title: Voltage-Service Flexumers: Physics-Constrained Learning and Conformal Safety Margins for Battery Energy Storage-Based Overvoltage Mitigation in Unbalanced Low-Voltage Networks
content: Single-phase photovoltaic inverters are a leading cause of overvoltage on long low-voltage (LV) feeders. A residential battery operated only for its owner, the prosumer, is usually full before the midday voltage peak and gives the feeder little relief. This paper develops the voltage-service flexumer (VSF), a prosumer battery operated for both self-consumption and voltage support, with a controller built from three components with proven properties: a ridge estimator of phase-resolved voltage sensitivities, with sign restrictions derived from the linearized four-wire power-flow equations, which is the projection of ordinary ridge regression onto a convex cone; a split-conformal safety margin with a joint, distribution-free coverage guarantee; and a state-of-charge-weighted linear program whose dual variables act as voltage shadow prices, complemented by an export-headroom reserve and a voltage-safe discharge rule. On a real unbalanced 20/0.4 kV network with 231 users and 58 prosumers, where the voltage exceeds 253 V in 124 of 672 intervals, the estimator reaches an out-of-sample error of 0.32 V, half that of a neural network, and the 2.0 V margin attains 95.6% coverage. With identical 10 kWh batteries, the prosumer leaves 74 overvoltage intervals, whereas the VSF removes all of them, without curtailment and without reducing the owners' self-consumption.
